blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Request logging writes every bearer token to the logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Never log credential headers (CWE-532): redact `Authorization` and `Cookie` (log the header name and, at most, a non-secret token identifier or prefix stored alongside the token) before logging, and make test `logs_requests` (tasks.md 1.3) assert the redaction. As designed, anyone with read access to the info-level logs (support staff, log pipeline, log storage backups) copies a live token from a log line and calls the API as that user; the same line also leaks the `session=` cookie that `src/http/middleware.rs` authenticates today. Because revocation is a Non-Goal, a token leaked this way cannot be invalidated, so the deferral makes the leak permanent.
findings.title: Request logging writes every bearer token to the logs

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store only a hash of the token (CWE-256/CWE-312): since tokens are 32 random bytes, a fast SHA-256 (or HMAC-SHA-256 with a server key) is enough and keeps the lookup an indexed equality on `token_hash`, so the stated performance reason for the clear storage does not hold. As designed, anyone who reads the `api_tokens` table — a SQL dump, a backup, a replica, a read-only SQL injection elsewhere — gets every user's live credential and can call the API as them, whereas passwords in the same database are bcrypt-hashed (`users.password_hash`). With no revocation, the exposure cannot be undone. Update tasks.md 1.1 and 1.2 accordingly.
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence: middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Looking up the hash of the presented token (see R-security-2) instead of the token itself removes any byte-by-byte timing signal from the index comparison; no separate fix is needed if R-security-2 is fixed. Whether the database comparison is observable remotely could not be verified.
findings.title: Token lookup by database equality may leak timing
